key_insight: A mixed s0/d0/d10 high-entropy perovskite electrolyte, (Ba0.50Sr0.50)(Ti0.33Zr0.33Sn0.33)O3, delivered the best solid oxide fuel cell performance by combining low leakage, low ohmic resistance, and favorable oxygen-ion/proton-conducting structure.
engineering_relevance: This work expands the electrolyte design space for solid oxide fuel cells by enabling rare-earth-free, high-entropy perovskite ceramics with improved conductivity and device power output.
method: Synthesized three high-entropy perovskite electrolytes via sequential sintering, high-pressure torsion processing, and calcination.
Printed ~6–10 μm electrolyte films on Ni–SrZr0.5Ce0.4Y0.1O3 anodes and coated Ba0.5La0.5CoO3 cathodes.
Compared electrochemical behavior with impedance spectroscopy plus synchrotron XAS and XPS to link structure with performance.
evidence_signal: The mixed s0/d0/d10 composition achieved the best result, with negligible current leakage, the lowest ohmic resistance, and a maximum power density of 0.53 W·cm−2 at 973 K.
watch_item: The reported performance is promising but still depends on careful control of microstructure, film thickness, and high-temperature processing, which may affect reproducibility and scale-up.
paper_title: High-entropy perovskites, architectured by s0/d0/d10 cations, as novel electrolytes for solid oxide fuel cells
